bible_refs.note: ἐὰν μή τις γεννηθῇ ἄνωθεν (3:3) joined with οὐ δύναται εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ (3:5); Cyril reads ὑμῖν for σοι.
Εἰ τὰ ἐπίγεια εἶπον ὑμῖν καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς ἐὰν εἴπω ὑμῖν τὰ ἐπουράνια πιστεύσετε; exact.
ὃ οἴδαμεν λαλοῦμεν καὶ ὃ ἑωράκαμεν μαρτυροῦμεν; Cyril ends οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει, the wording of John 3:32, for John 3:11 οὐ λαμβάνετε.
LXX καὶ τὰ ἐν χερσὶν εὑρίσκομεν μετὰ πόνου; Cyril reads μετὰ βίας.
Lemma Πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ' αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται.
πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου σωθήσεται (Paul quoting Joel 2:32, LXX Joel 3:5).
ἀνακεφαλαιοῦσθαι τὰ πάντα ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ echoes ἀνακεφαλαιώσασθαι τὰ πάντα ἐν τῷ Χριστῷ.
Lemma Μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ; μὴ γένοιτο; also the paraphrase Ἰσραηλίτην καὶ ἐκ σπέρματος Ἁβραάμ.
τέθειται ... κήρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος εἰς τὰ ἔθνη echoes ἐτέθην ἐγὼ κῆρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος ... διδάσκαλος ἐθνῶν.
οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ, and the lemma Ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφή;
Ahab reigning in Samaria and Israel's idol worship (LXX 3 Kingdoms 16:29–33); Cyril summarizes the history, no verbal quotation.

pass_a_gloss: [ὁ μὲν γὰρ, end of u09-rem-mid] our Lord Jesus Christ once to Nicodemus set before (παρετίθει) the words about spiritual regeneration (ἀναγέννησις) and said: amen amen I say to you (pl.), unless one is born from above (ἄνωθεν), he is not able to enter into the kingdom (βασιλεία) of God; [then added to these the following]. but he understanding (συνίημι) nothing at all, then indeed Christ, placing the thickness (πάχος) of human understanding (διάνοια) as far as possible from the thinness/fineness (ἰσχνότης) of the concepts (ἔννοιαι): if earthly things (ἐπίγεια) I said to you and you do not believe, how if I say to you heavenly things (ἐπουράνια) will you believe? and added: amen amen I say to you, what we know we speak and what we have seen we testify (μαρτυροῦμεν), and our testimony (μαρτυρία) no one receives. therefore untested/not-to-be-examined (ἀβασάνιστα) the things above us; for if it is true that the things in hands we find with force/difficulty (μετὰ βίας), according to the written, how not necessary to think that in things above reason (ὑπὲρ λόγον) faith (πίστις) is very most useful, no search (ἔρευνα) following, no random seeking (ζήτησις εἰκαία) brought on? for by understanding (σύνεσις) such matters are brilliantly honoured (τιμᾶται). LEMMA: everyone believing on him will not be put to shame (καταισχυνθήσεται) etc. let not Israel make salvation through faith a private good (ἴδιον ἀγαθόν); for everyone who calls on (ἐπικαλέσηται) the name of the Lord will be saved, whether Jew or Greek, slave or free; indifferently/without distinction (ἀδιαφόρως) the God of the whole saves, for all things are his; thus we say all things are summed up (ἀνακεφαλαιοῦσθαι) in Christ. LEMMA: did God push away (ἀπώσατο) his people? may it not be. prudently (ἐμφρόνως) Paul, although [Israel] having suffered the darkening (σκοτισμός), does not let Israel be more hardened (κατασκληρύνεσθαι) by total despairs (ἀπογνώσεσι), but goes after [them] as with art (ἐντέχνως) by kind words (χρηστοέπεια). for just now he accused Israel as disobedient (ἀπειθής); yet does not strip [it] of hope from above, nor says it was wholly thrust out (ἐξωσθῆναι) from kinship/closeness (οἰκειότης) to God. and makes clear proof (ἀπόδειξις) of the matter, setting forth himself being an Israelite and from the seed of Abraham, and most aptly (εὐφυέστατα) still calling [them] people of God, and adding 'may it not be' to the words about being pushed away. these were as of one fawning on (περισαίνοντος) those who chose to disobey, and flatteringly (θωπικῶς) running under/coming round, and carrying them to a pious and docile (εὐήνιον) disposition (ἕξις). if then it is evident that he himself has been called to apostleship (ἀποστολή), and placed as sacred minister (ἱερουργός) of the Saviour's mysteries (μυστήρια), herald (κήρυξ) and apostle to the nations, though being from Israel, it is very clear that God did not push away his people. LEMMA: or do you not know in Elijah what the scripture says? most timely (ἐπικαιρότατα), as an image (εἰκών) of what befell Israel, he brings in the history (ἱστορία) about Elijah; for it is possible from the likeness of the affairs of that time easily to see that Israel itself acted drunkenly/outrageously (πεπαροίνηκεν) against itself; for Ahab reigning over Samaria, extraordinarily (ἐκτόπως) the hand-cut things (χειρότμητα) were worshipped (ἐθρησκεύετο) by Israel, and there were sacrifices and precincts (τεμένη) everywhere; and those attached (προσκείμενοι) to God feared entirely, and unbearable (δύσοιστον) [broken off]
pass_b_english: …our Lord Jesus Christ once set before Nicodemus the words about spiritual rebirth, and he said, “Truly, truly, I say to you, unless one is born from above, he cannot enter the kingdom of God” (John 3:3, 5). [Then he added to these the words that follow.] But when Nicodemus understood nothing at all, then indeed Christ, showing how far the dullness of the human mind stands from the fineness of these thoughts, says, “If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?” (John 3:12). And to these he added, “Truly, truly, I say to you, we speak of what we know and bear witness to what we have seen, and no one receives our testimony” (John 3:11).

So the things that are beyond us are not to be put to the test. For if it is true that “we find with difficulty the things that are in our hands,” as it is written (Wisdom of Solomon 9:16), how can we not see that, in matters beyond reason at least, faith is of the greatest use, with no inquiry following after it and no idle questioning brought to bear? For it is by understanding that matters of this kind are splendidly honoured.

“Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame” (Romans 10:11), and the rest. Let Israel not make salvation through faith its own private good. For, he says, “everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved” (Romans 10:13), whether he is a Jew or a Greek, a slave or free. The God of all saves without distinction, for all things are his. In this sense we say that all things are summed up in Christ (Ephesians 1:10).

“Has God rejected his people? By no means” (Romans 11:1). Paul acts wisely. Although Israel had suffered the darkening, he does not let it be hardened still further by utter despair, but he goes after it, as it were, with skill and with kind words. For just now he was accusing Israel of disobedience; yet he does not strip it of the hope that comes from above, nor does he say that it has been wholly thrust out of its closeness to God.

And he makes the proof of the matter plain by setting himself forward as an Israelite and of the seed of Abraham (Romans 11:1). Most aptly, too, he still calls them God’s people, and he adds “By no means” to the words about being rejected. This was the act of one who, as it were, gently wins over those who had chosen to disobey, coming round them with coaxing words and bringing them to a devout and teachable habit of mind. If, then, it is evident that he himself has been called to apostleship, and has been appointed a minister of the sacred mysteries of the Saviour, a herald and apostle to the nations (1 Timothy 2:7), although he is from Israel, it is plain that “God has not rejected his people” (Romans 11:2).

“Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the story of Elijah?” (Romans 11:2). Most fittingly he brings in the account of Elijah as a kind of picture of what had happened to Israel. For from the likeness of the events of that time one can easily see that Israel itself has acted outrageously, to its own harm. When Ahab reigned over Samaria, things carved by hand were worshipped by Israel beyond all bounds, and there were sacrifices and sacred precincts everywhere (1 Kings 16:29–33). Those who held fast to God were utterly afraid, and so hard to bear…

Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς Νικοδήμῳ ποτὲ τοὺς περὶ τῆς πνευματικῆς
ἀναγεννήσεως παρετίθει λόγους καὶ δὴ καὶ ἔφασκεν "Ἀμὴν "ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν μή τις
γεννηθῇ ἄνωθεν, οὐ δύναται "εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ·" [εἶτα τούτοις
προσετίθει τὰ ἐφεξῆς]. συνιέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ παντελῶς οὐδὲν, τότε δὴ τότε Χριστὸς τῆς
τῶν ἐννοιῶν ἰσχνότητος ὡς ἀπωτάτω τιθεὶς τῆς ἀνθρώπου διανοίας τὸ πάχος "Εἰ τὰ
ἐπίγεια εἶπον 237 "ὑμῖν, φησὶ, καὶ οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς ἐὰν εἴπω ὑμῖν τὰ ἐπου"ράνια
πιστεύσετε;" προσετίθει δὲ τούτοις "Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν "λέγω ὑμῖν ὃ οἴδαμεν λαλοῦμεν καὶ ὃ
ἑωράκαμεν μαρτυροῦμεν καὶ τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἡμῶν οὐδεὶς λαμβάνει." οὐκοῦν
ἀβασάνιστα τὰ ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς· εἰ γάρ ἐστιν ἀληθὲς ὅτι περ "τὰ ἐν χερσὶν εὑρίσκομεν μετὰ
βίας," κατὰ τὸ γεγραμμένον, πῶς οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον ἐννοεῖν, ὡς ἔν γε τοῖς ὑπὲρ λόγον,
χρησιμωτάτη λίαν ἡ πίστις, οὐκ ἀκολουθούσης ἐρεύνης, οὐ ζητήσεως εἰκαίας
ἐπενηνεγμένης; συνέσει γὰρ τὰ τοιάδε τῶν πραγμάτων τιμᾶται λαμπρῶς. Πᾶς ὁ
πιστεύων ἐπ' αὐτῷ οὐ καταισχυνθήσεται κ.τ.λ. Μὴ ποιείσθω ἴδιον ἀγαθὸν τὴν διὰ
πίστεως σωτηρίαν ὁ Ἰσραήλ· πᾶς γὰρ ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηταί φησι τὸ ὄνομα Κυρίου
σωθήσεται, κἂν ἰουδαῖος ᾖ κἂν ἕλλην, κἂν δοῦλος κἂν ἐλεύθερος· ἀδιαφόρως σώζει ὁ
Θεὸς τῶν ὅλων, αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἅπαντα· οὕτω φαμὲν ἀνακεφαλαιοῦσθαι τὰ πάντα ἐν τῷ
Χριστῷ.
Μὴ ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ; μὴ γένοιτο. Ἐμφρόνως ὁ Παῦλος καίτοι
παθόντα τὸν σκοτισμὸν οὐκ ἐᾷ μειζόνως κατασκληρύνεσθαι τὸν Ἰσραὴλ ταῖς εἰς ἅπαν
ἀπογνώσεσι, μέτεισι δὲ ὥσπερ ἐντέχνως ταῖς χρηστοεπείαις. ἄρτι μὲν γὰρ ὡς ἀπειθῆ
κατῃτιᾶτο τὸν Ἰσραήλ· ἐλπίδος γεμὴν τῆς ἄνωθεν οὐκ ἀπογυμνοῖ, οὔτε μὴν ὁλοτρόπως
τῆς πρὸς Θεὸν οἰκειότητος ἐξωσθῆναί φησι. καὶ σαφῆ τοῦ πράγματος ποιεῖται τὴν
ἀπόδειξιν, ἑαυτὸν παραθεὶς ὄντα Ἰσραηλίτην καὶ ἐκ σπέρματος Ἁβραὰμ, εὐφυέστατά τε
καὶ Θεοῦ λαὸν ἀποκαλῶν ἔτι, καὶ προστιθεὶς τό Μὴ γένοιτο τοῖς περὶ τοῦ ἀπεῶσθαι
λόγοις. ταῦτα δὲ ἦν οἱονεὶ περισαίνοντος τοὺς 238 ἀπειθεῖν ἑλομένους, καὶ θωπικῶς
ὑποτρέχοντος, καὶ εἰς ἕξιν αὐτοὺς ἀποφέροντος τὴν εὐσεβῆ καὶ εὐήνιον. εἴπερ οὖν ἐστιν
ἐναργὲς ὡς κέκληται πρὸς ἀποστολὴν αὐτὸς, τέθειται δὲ καὶ τῶν τοῦ Σωτῆρος
μυστηρίων ἱερουργὸς, εἰς τὰ ἔθνη κήρυξ καὶ ἀπόστολος, καίτοι ὑπάρχων ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ,
πρόδηλον ὡς οὐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ Θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ. Ἢ οὐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ
γραφή; Ἐπικαιρότατα καθάπερ εἰκόνα τινὰ τοῦ συμβεβηκότος τῷ Ἰσραὴλ παρακομίζει
τὴν ἱστορίαν τὴν ἐπὶ τῷ Ἠλιοῦ· ἔστι γὰρ ὡς ἐξ ὁμοιότητος τῶν τὸ τηνικάδε πραγμάτων
κατιδεῖν εὐκόλως, ὡς αὐτὸς ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ πεπαροίνηκεν ὁ Ἰσραήλ· βασιλεύοντος μὲν γὰρ
Ἀχαὰβ τῆς Σαμαρείας, ἐκτόπως ἐθρησκεύετο τὰ χειρότμητα παρὰ τοῦ Ἰσραὴλ, θυσίαι τε
ἦσαν καὶ τεμένη πανταχοῦ· ἐδεδίεσαν δὲ πάντως οἱ Θεῷ προσκείμενοι καὶ δύσοιστον

review_notes: Fixed in place in tr9.json. (1) Join with u10-open was wrong: καὶ δύσοιστον goes with τὴν δίωξιν and the οὕτω…ὡς clause that opens u10-open ('so hard to bear was the persecution they endured that prophets even hid…'), so the cut now reads 'and so hard to bear…', not 'and an unbearable…' (which left no noun to land on). Translator note on the join updated. (2) Divine pronouns He/Him/His were upper case here but lower case in every other staged row of this book (tr0–tr4, tr6–tr8) and in the u09-rem-early/mid rows of the same file; set to lower case. (3) 'has done outrage against itself' was stiff; πεπαροίνηκεν ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ now 'has acted outrageously, to its own harm'. Rest checked clause by clause; citations correct (Wisdom of Solomon 9:16 with Cyril's μετὰ βίας; John 3:11 wording noted).
Opens mid-sentence: ὁ μὲν γὰρ ('For ...') stands at the end of u09-rem-mid; the leading ellipsis marks the join.

Ends mid-sentence at καὶ δύσοιστον, which governs τὴν δίωξιν in u10-open (δύσοιστον οὕτω τὴν δίωξιν ὑπομεμενήκασιν, ὡς…: 'so hard to bear was the persecution they endured that…'). Rendered 'and so hard to bear…'; u10-open resumes '…was the persecution they endured that…'. Nothing supplied.
The bracketed clause [εἶτα τούτοις προσετίθει τὰ ἐφεξῆς] is bracketed in the copy-text and kept in brackets.
PG column numbers 237 and 238 and the page number 27 in the copy-text are dropped from the reading text.
συνιέντος δὲ αὐτοῦ: the subject is Nicodemus; named in English for clarity.

τῆς τῶν ἐννοιῶν ἰσχνότητος ὡς ἀπωτάτω τιθεὶς τῆς ἀνθρώπου διανοίας τὸ πάχος: literally 'placing the thickness of human understanding as far as possible from the fineness of the concepts'; rendered 'showing how far the dullness of the human mind stands from the fineness of these thoughts'.
ἀβασάνιστα: 'not to be examined, not to be put to the test'; Cyril means the things beyond us are not to be probed.
συνέσει ... τιμᾶται λαμπρῶς: dative of means, 'are splendidly honoured by understanding'; the sense is that wise understanding honours such matters by not prying.

κἂν δοῦλος κἂν ἐλεύθερος: possible echo of Galatians 3:28 or Colossians 3:11; left uncited in the reading text as uncertain. Romans 10:12 ('no distinction between Jew and Greek') stands behind ἀδιαφόρως.
ἄρτι μὲν γὰρ ὡς ἀπειθῆ κατῃτιᾶτο: refers back to Paul's charge in Romans 10:21 ('a disobedient and contrary people'); a possible reference, not cited inline.

περισαίνοντος ... θωπικῶς ὑποτρέχοντος: literally 'fawning upon ... flatteringly running up to'; Cyril uses the words in praise of Paul's tact, rendered 'gently wins over ... coming round them with coaxing words'.
ἱερουργός: echoes Romans 15:16 (ἱερουργοῦντα τὸ εὐαγγέλιον); possible, noted only.
πεπαροίνηκεν ἐφ' ἑαυτῷ: 'has behaved outrageously (as in drunken violence) against himself'; rendered 'has acted outrageously, to its own harm'.
Israel is treated as a singular collective in the Greek; English uses 'it', and 'them' where Cyril shifts to τὸν λαόν.
